dominant_breach: housing-loss records blocking future housing, credit, and recovery entry

fresh_start_capacity_gate.note: A housing shock is not recoverable if eviction, foreclosure, and credit records continue to deny future units, loans, deposits, or insurance after the crisis.

foreclosure_loss_mitigation.note: Loss-mitigation procedures are useful only if they pause foreclosure long enough, include language/offline access, and produce sustainable outcomes before sale.

eviction_foreclosure_record_sealing.note: Sealing/relief must reach courts, brokers, tenant-screening vendors, and credit/specialty reports; court relief alone is insufficient.

record_afterlife_housing_entry.note: Negative record afterlife must be scored by how long records block leases, mortgages, insurance, deposits, and employment after the legal dispute ends.

vendor_record_suppression_after_clearanc.note: The case requires proof that private vendors suppress or correct records after sealing, dismissal, satisfaction, or foreclosure-avoidance resolution.

proof_debt: eviction/foreclosure record sealing implementation and vendor propagation
time from housing shock to lease or mortgage reentry
foreclosure loss-mitigation timing before irreversible sale
credit and specialty-report cleanup after housing relief

gate_18_fresh_start_capacity.why: Comfort certification is blocked until the scoreboard proves claim conversion, notice, timing, legal aid or administrative capacity, vendor/report suppression where relevant, and subgroup outcomes at the actual threshold moment.

evidence_debt_register.question: foreclosure loss-mitigation timing before irreversible sale
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Track whether assistance, review, language access, and appeals halt foreclosure before sale, credit harm, or displacement.

evidence_debt_register.question: credit and specialty-report cleanup after housing relief
evidence_debt_register.next_evidence: Pair court relief with consumer-reporting dispute evidence and adverse-action reason tests.

remedy_operability_register.harm_or_claim: Housing-loss record blocks reentry after eviction, foreclosure, or delinquency
remedy_operability_register.claimant_perimeter: Tenants, homeowners, and families with dismissed, sealed, satisfied, cured, or loss-mitigated housing records
remedy_operability_register.standing_path: Court sealing/expungement, servicer appeal, FCRA dispute, housing agency complaint, and fair-housing/consumer action
remedy_operability_register.notice_explanation: Notice must identify which public/private records will remain and how to correct them
remedy_operability_register.interim_protection: Stay of eviction/foreclosure or record-suppression bridge during pending relief
remedy_operability_register.time_to_relief: Before application denial, sheriff sale, displacement, or rental/mortgage adverse action
remedy_operability_register.review_body: Housing court, mortgage servicer, HUD/CFPB/state housing agency, consumer-reporting agency
remedy_operability_register.collective_or_representative_action: Legal aid, tenant unions, housing agencies, AG/CFPB enforcement, fair-housing organizations
remedy_operability_register.restoration_remedy: Sealing, correction, suppression, foreclosure alternative, reinstatement, lease/mortgage reconsideration
remedy_operability_register.enforcement_actor: Courts, servicers, HUD/CFPB, CRAs, tenant-screening vendors
